name: Josephinism
summary: Josephinism is the programme of enlightened absolutism pursued by Joseph II in the Habsburg lands (1780-90). It sought a unitary, centralised, rational and largely secular state run by merit-appointed officials, with the Catholic church placed under state control, limited toleration for non-Catholics and Jews, reform of serfdom, compulsory schooling and uniform law and taxation, all imposed from above by the monarch's edicts.
scope: Joseph II's domestic policy as a governing doctrine, with its roots under Maria Theresa and Chancellor Kaunitz. Based on the Josephine edicts (Toleration Patent 1781, Edict for the Jews of Lower Austria 1782, Serfdom Patent 1781, Marriage Patent 1783, 1787 penal code) as described by historians. It excludes later Austrian 'Josephinism' as a bureaucratic tradition and Joseph's foreign policy except where it bears on centralisation. Most modern topics are anachronistic and answered by inference at low confidence.

missingStatements.text: Bishops and clergy should answer to the state rather than to a foreign religious authority.
missingStatements.rationale: Austrian bishops were barred from direct communication with the Curia and clergy were trained in state seminaries.

missingStatements.text: Contemplative religious orders that do no teaching, nursing or other useful work should be dissolved and their property used for public purposes.
missingStatements.rationale: Joseph dissolved over 500 monasteries and used the proceeds for parishes and welfare institutions.

missingStatements.text: A ruler may legitimately decree sweeping reforms for the people's good without their or their representatives' consent.
missingStatements.rationale: Joseph issued thousands of edicts and bypassed diets in the belief that reason would swiftly yield the best results.

notes: Rational reform from above by a Catholic monarch who curbed the church. Scholars dispute whether 'Josephinism' is a coherent doctrine, and Joseph withdrew many measures under resistance before his death in 1790. Toleration was partial (limited worship, restrictions on Jews) and censorship was relaxed then tightened.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Joseph centralised medical care in the Vienna General Hospital (1784) as a state project; a state-provided universal scheme is inferred from that paternalist welfare-state activism, not stated.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage-setting was not a Josephine issue; a cameralist ruler concerned with state revenue and a productive populace gives no clear lean.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Josephine policy was cameralist and state-directed (uniform taxes, state-run reforms); markets were not trusted to order society, though trade was encouraged. Inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: No programme of nationalising industry; the state did seize monastic property but for religious and charity funds, not industry. Inferred neutral.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Joseph ordered a uniform land valuation and equal land tax to make the nobility pay a fair share, though the 1789 tax decree was withdrawn at his death.

unions-good.rationale: Guild and corporate bodies were curtailed in favour of a uniform state under the sovereign's control; unions are an anachronism, inferred from distrust of intermediate bodies.

property-fundamental.rationale: Joseph overrode noble and church property when state interest required: monasteries were dissolved and a new land valuation imposed.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations in the modern sense did not exist; mercantilist state regulation of trade was normal, so a mild lean is inferred but not stated.

cut-welfare.rationale: Dissolved monastery wealth funded about 1,700 parishes and welfare institutions, showing the state took charge of poor relief rather than cutting it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Reform aimed at tenant peasants paying rent and being freed from lords, not at collective ownership of enterprises; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A centralised, paternalist state that pursued security and uniformity would accept surveillance, though the issue itself is anachronistic.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not an issue of the period; a paternalist state regulating morals gives no clear answer.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Censorship was limited to material that blasphemed, subverted government or promoted immorality, but hate speech as such was not addressed.

strong-leader.rationale: Joseph ruled as an absolute monarch who issued thousands of edicts and believed reason would quickly yield results; bypassing estates and diets was central to the method.

state-harmful.rationale: Josephinism sought an efficient, unitary, centralised state to remake society; the state is the engine of reform, never an evil.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position; a disciplined centralising state would lean to control, but this is not discussed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Joseph expanded the army and pursued war with the Ottomans and over Bavaria, and built a centralised bureaucracy; police power is inferred from this.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The state policed immorality through censorship limits and a paternalist moral order; a legal-sex-work answer is inferred from that, not stated.

decide-locally.rationale: Josephinism centralised administration, replaced Hungarian Latin with German, moved the crowns to Vienna and overrode local diets; Hungarians and Belgians revolted against this.

rehabilitation.rationale: The 1787 penal code replaced capital punishment with harsh imprisonment and restored some severe penalties, treating punishment as deterrent and useful labour rather than rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Joseph made marriage a civil contract and gave daughters equal inheritance, yet remained a Catholic who favoured population growth; split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Unconsidered in the period; Josephine law punished same-sex acts and marriage was civil heterosexual contract. Inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not discussed in sources opened; a populationist, Catholic-influenced Enlightened ruler would oppose. Inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Joseph opposed contemplative orders, dissolved over 500 monasteries and subordinated clergy to the state, aiming for a mostly secular society, though he was a Catholic.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not an issue of the era; the Jewish edict aimed at making Jews useful to the state rather than redressing injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; equal inheritance for sons and daughters was introduced but no theory of gender is documented.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Joseph pushed German as the administrative and school language across the multi-ethnic monarchy, overriding local traditions for uniformity.

gradual-change.rationale: Joseph issued thousands of edicts in a top-down programme of rapid reform and tolerated little deference to established institutions or custom.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Habsburg cameralism valued population growth, though Joseph he restricted Jewish settlement numbers in Vienna. Inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anachronistic; a sovereigntist emperor focused on state power would not cede authority, inferred from his unitary-state aims.

free-trade.rationale: Habsburg economic policy was mercantilist; a partly protective regime is inferred rather than cited directly.

nation-first.rationale: Joseph pursued Habsburg territorial and dynastic interests (Bavaria, the Ottoman war) without much regard to international cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign policy was dynastic and expansionist; intervention for human rights is anachronistic.

open-borders.rationale: A cameralist state controlling settlement, as in the edict freezing the number of tolerated Jewish families, would reject open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Cameralist and Enlightenment thought sought greater production and population; limits to growth for environmental reasons are anachronistic.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; a paternalist state would act, but there is no source basis.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Enlightened rationalism and belief that reason would swiftly improve life supports optimism about progress and science, inferred for technology specifically.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic with no basis for an answer; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Joseph believed in reform from above by the monarch and his officials and met the unrest his reforms provoked with withdrawal or tightened censorship, never with endorsement of revolt.

experts-over-public.rationale: Officials were promoted by merit and legally trained, and reform was designed by enlightened officials for the people rather than with them.

central-planning.rationale: The state planned reform in detail but stayed within a cameralist, property-owning economy; a fully planned economy is anachronistic.

socialized-markets.rationale: No basis in the sources; the question belongs to later debates.

land-value-tax.rationale: Joseph ordered a new appraisal of all land to create a single equal land tax, though it was not meant to replace all other taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed; a fiscal reformer might favour, but no evidence.

basic-income.rationale: Poor relief was organised through state and parish institutions funded from monastery property; unconditional income is anachronistic.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Habsburg mercantilism used protective tariffs and prohibitions; inferred from the general cameralist pattern rather than a source opened.

state-directs-investment.rationale: A cameralist state that founded factories and urged others, including Jews, to found manufactures, would direct investment; stated loosely in the 1782 edict.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Serfdom reform let peasants buy hereditary ownership of their land and aimed at rent-paying tenancy, spreading small holdings.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Josephine state sought tax revenue, uniform accounting and a money economy; abolishing money is wholly alien. Inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Anachronistic; the state's fiscal control under Joseph (uniform accounting) suggests no wish to leave money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Joseph curtailed estates and corporate privileges in favour of direct state control, so state-recognised bodies setting wages and prices cuts against his unitary design.

one-party-rule.rationale: Anachronistic; Joseph rejected representative bodies, but ruled through monarchy and bureaucracy, not a party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Joseph II was an absolute hereditary monarch and the model of enlightened absolutism; Josephinism takes monarchy as the vehicle of reform.

democracy-best.rationale: Reform was for the people but not by them; the monarch decided and diets were bypassed, so democracy was not valued.

direct-votes.rationale: Rule by edict and distrust of estates and diets make popular votes on laws foreign to Josephinism.

workers-councils.rationale: Power was concentrated in the monarch and a bureaucracy; councils of workers are alien and anachronistic.

right-to-secede.rationale: Joseph centralised the realm and crushed or ignored local autonomy; the Belgian revolt against his reforms was a secession attempt he opposed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Officials were promoted by merit, yet Joseph held that the enlightened monarch was uniquely placed to know what is best for subjects; moderately inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Joseph waged wars and pursued reform by decree, but no principle on political violence is documented.

war-builds-character.rationale: Enlightened rationalism did not glorify war, though Joseph fought dynastic wars; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The state governed the church: bishops could not deal directly with Rome and clergy were trained in state seminaries, so strict separation was the opposite of Josephinism.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The state aimed at a rational and mostly secular legal order, treating marriage as a civil contract (1783) rather than a religious one.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Joseph centralised the judiciary, made the supreme court independent and cut appellate courts to six; private justice was abolished as noble jurisdiction was curtailed.

military-superiority.rationale: Joseph expanded territory and fought the Ottomans and over Bavaria, which suggests desire for Habsburg strength; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Habsburg realm was multi-ethnic and Joseph sought a unitary state of subjects, not a nation of one ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Reform from above aimed at harmonising orders under the monarch, with no theory of class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Joseph never moved to overcome social differences; he sought more equality before the law but left the social hierarchy intact.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic; a unitary state would resist devolved authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anachronistic with no basis; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

civilizational-union.rationale: The state aimed at unity of the Habsburg lands, not union by religion or civilization across borders; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Enlightened cameralism stressed service to the state and public welfare, with the ruler as first servant of the state.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The monarch regarded himself as servant of the state, and subjects were to serve its ends; inferred as a rough lean.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No documented view; instrumental Enlightenment attitudes to nature are inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Cameralist states generally sought population growth for taxes and soldiers; inferred from the school and not from an opened source.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Joseph encouraged manufactures and trades, as the 1782 edict exhorting factory founding shows.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Joseph was a rapid reformer, but technology as such was not a stated goal.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; his rational-bureaucratic ideal is a distant analogue, so not strongly opposed.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A centralising state with censorship powers would not welcome citizen secrecy; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Josephinism broke with feudal institutions, dissolved monasteries and changed law and language, in favour of a rational and more equal order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Joseph believed reason would quickly produce the best results and reversed measures that failed, though his reforms were ideologically driven.

direct-action.rationale: Change came from the monarch's decrees and not from popular action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Joseph imposed liberal ends by absolute means, so adherents would not endorse this; no explicit view.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly foreign to an Enlightenment cameralist ruler.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Joseph encouraged crafts, trades and manufactures; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Poor relief was funded from monastery assets, but income by work and rank was retained; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Joseph encouraged manufactures and trades for state revenue; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: No such theory existed; the state encouraged business.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Power remained with the monarch and privileged orders were reformed, not overthrown by a class.

collective-farming.rationale: Serf reform aimed at individual peasant ownership or rent-paying tenancy, not collective farms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Joseph's own wars were dynastic; no capitalist theory of war is documented.

taxation-theft.rationale: Joseph sought a uniform, equal land tax to raise state revenue and spread the burden, treating taxation as legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: The state regulated religious life and morality and curtailed worship and building by non-Catholics, rather than limiting itself to preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The state granted civil rights as concessions from the sovereign but the enlightened monarch held community and state duties as central; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Habsburg armies relied on conscription; inferred from standard practice rather than from an opened source.

exit-over-voice.rationale: A state that centralised power and restricted settlement and movement did not see exit as the check; Joseph's own subjects' emigration was discouraged.

state-as-business.rationale: Joseph stressed state revenue and uniform accounting but the state was a paternal sovereign, not a firm; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Joseph wanted to improve subjects' lives by education, scholarships for poor students and health care, a paternal version of material enabling.

media-academia-power.rationale: Joseph tightened or relaxed censorship at will, showing state control of the press; no theory of media power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Joseph's toleration edicts aimed to integrate groups into the state; scientific racism is anachronistic.

organic-representation.rationale: Joseph bypassed estates and diets, the traditional bodies of representation, to govern directly through officials.

total-state.rationale: Josephinism put education, church, marriage, medicine and the economy under state direction, though it did not claim to direct culture totally.

national-rebirth.rationale: Joseph's reform was rational modernisation, not a rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Joseph pursued expansion, notably in Bavaria, and joined Russia in the 1788 Ottoman war.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Joseph replaced personal and estate ties with merit-based officials and direct state authority, and weakened lordly control over serfs.

bound-labor.rationale: The 1781 Serfdom Patent abolished lordly control over marriage, movement and occupation, aiming to replace forced labour with rent-paying tenancy.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Enlightenment rationalism held knowledge was reason's discovery; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Enlightened reason as a source of common rules for all subjects is inferred, though not directly stated in the sources opened.

single-common-good.rationale: Joseph sought a single rational order for the state's welfare, overriding estate interests, with the monarch determining it.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Joseph wanted Jews to serve the Habsburg state and assimilate, which is inconsistent with a separate state; anachronistic.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

revive-national-language.rationale: Joseph replaced Latin with German as administrative and school language rather than reviving local tongues.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Governance was by the sovereign and officials; democratic control of firms is anachronistic.

school-vouchers.rationale: Elementary education was made compulsory and priestly education was moved into state seminaries, reflecting state control over schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Joseph sought uniform accounting and fiscal discipline, though wars strained finances; inferred and anachronistic.

economic-freedom.rationale: He eased some restrictions on trades for Jews and others, but liberal political freedom was not seen as dependent on it.

rule-by-example.rationale: Joseph ruled by thousands of edicts and laws, not by moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Josephinism built a unitary, German-administered state against Hungarian and Belgian demands to keep their own institutions.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The ideal was a rational and mostly secular society, though Joseph was personally Catholic and did not make reason the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Dissolved monastic wealth funded welfare institutions but eligibility rules for foreigners are not documented.

work-for-welfare.rationale: A cameralist state that favoured useful work and dissolved orders that contributed nothing to society would favour work conditions; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Joseph aimed to harmonise orders under the throne, with nobles, peasants and burghers serving the state, rather than class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Joseph opened the Prater and Augarten to the public and supported Mozart, but dissolved monasteries; cultural heritage was not a target.

dominated-front.rationale: Anachronistic; irrelevant to a Habsburg emperor.

workers-nation.rationale: A workers' national organisation is anachronistic; Joseph sought a supranational state.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Joseph introduced equal inheritance for sons and daughters, but public life was male-run; split.

ban-interest.rationale: The 1782 edict permitted lending against real estate and encouraged manufactures and trades, so state economics assumed credit.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Joseph's edicts removed discriminatory marks and widened schooling and trades for Jews, rejecting legal segregation, although they kept some limits.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Josephinism presented the state as an impartial rational agent above orders, even curbing nobles.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Jewish edict made German replace Hebrew and Yiddish in official use and urged Jews into state schools, expecting assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in Josephinism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Joseph bypassed representative bodies, so electoral design was not an issue; slight lean against.

national-mission.rationale: Joseph's reforms were aimed at his own realm rather than at exporting a political form.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: No documented view; equal inheritance suggests partial reform.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Joseph criticised the privileged orders and clerics as useless but not corrupt per se; split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Anachronistic; Joseph's reforms favoured population and public health, not eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: A sovereign controlling his own forces would not accept legal accountability for them; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Joseph's state extended into education, health, church, marriage and the economy, the opposite of a night-watchman state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Habsburg approach pushed assimilation of minorities; discouragement of mixing is not documented.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Joseph introduced equal treatment before courts, ended noble court privileges and widened rights for non-Catholics and Jews, but kept social differences.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Joseph encouraged colonisation of his territories; no such critique existed.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Joseph introduced civil marriage and equal law for all subjects, with a unified judicial system and equal treatment of offenders.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Joseph allowed non-Catholics to practise but conversion rules and mixed marriage were regulated; no clear ban on conversion.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Schools and seminaries were taken over by the state, but religious instruction in elementary schooling persisted under the established Catholic framework.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority rested on the monarch's rational judgement, not on consent; reform was for the people but not by them.

trade-surplus.rationale: Habsburg mercantilist outlook suggests it, but inferred and not from the sources opened.

population-transfer.rationale: Joseph pressed for assimilation of Jews, not expulsion except for serious misconduct; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Joseph waged war and used state coercion extensively.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The ideal was rational state-led reform and harmony of orders.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Anachronistic; Joseph tolerated no organised opposition but had no parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Joseph held arbitrary absolute power over his subjects, though he used it benevolently.

separated-powers.rationale: Joseph made the supreme court independent and required trained judges but kept all powers in the monarch's hands.

vanguard-party.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Monastery wealth funded welfare, but a general priority of the poor was not a governing principle.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: A state that dissolved intermediate bodies would probably limit strikes; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Cameralism saw population as wealth, and Joseph blamed feudal institutions for peasant burden.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Joseph governed a diverse monarchy and wanted uniformity by law and language, not homogeneity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Posts were filled by merit and legal training.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: An absolute monarch can set aside rules; Joseph tightened censorship under unrest.

party-controls-media.rationale: Joseph centralised and varied censorship, but no party existed; split.

party-commands-army.rationale: Anachronistic; the monarch commanded the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: No documented view of citizenship waiting periods; the edicts froze tolerated Jewish families in Vienna but set no naturalisation rule.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Joseph pursued unitary sovereignty and resisted local diets; anachronistic.

head-commands-forces.rationale: As emperor Joseph commanded the army and appointed ministers himself; absolute rule is the core of Josephine government.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The church remained Catholic and episcopal, but bishops were bound to the state and denied direct contact with the Curia.

clerical-rule.rationale: The state subjected clergy to civil authority and dissolved orders.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship was limited to blasphemy, sedition and immorality, which fits the statement partly while greatly reduced.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

recall-officials.rationale: Officials answered to the monarch, not voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Joseph used the Russian alliance and wars; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The 1782 edict allowed Jews to rent in cities and assumed property rights; abolition of renting is alien.

people-in-arms.rationale: Joseph relied on a standing army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Peasant reform helped the countryside, yet Joseph built central hospitals and cities in Vienna.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Habsburg concern was dynastic; nationalism was alien.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Josephinism relied on educated officials and expanded education.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: German was treated as the language of administration and learning, implying a hierarchy of cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: The 1787 penal code effectively abolished capital punishment in favour of harsh imprisonment, with executions rare from 1783.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: A rationalist school system would reject this; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Censorship allowed under Joseph covered material promoting immorality.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

minority-language-support.rationale: Joseph imposed German as administrative and school language, replacing Latin and provoking Hungarian resistance.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Non-Catholics got tolerance with limits, and the edicts required German records and schooling despite Jewish custom.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Joseph aimed at uniformity, with state-set norms.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anachronistic; a fiscal reformer would honour debts.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The monarch decreed the legal order and did not convene diets.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Joseph restricted political liberties while expanding material reforms, though censorship later tightened.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The emperor was hereditary monarch, so election of the head of state is excluded.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Anachronistic; finances were managed by the crown's officials.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Anachronistic; dynastic diplomacy traded territory freely.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Joseph confiscated monastic property for religion and charity funds and reshaped lord-peasant relations in the state's interest.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, so left neutral or inferred from his general programme of centralised, rational monarchy.

collective-defense.rationale: Joseph used the Russian alliance, but the collective-defence principle is not documented.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Joseph sought to annex Bavaria without consent of the inhabitants; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Bishops could not communicate directly with Rome, over 500 monasteries were dissolved, and the state took control of priestly education.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Joseph was an active ruler who made policy himself, not a symbolic head.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Joseph centralised the monarchy and resisted Belgian and Hungarian resistance, though he later backed down in part.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The programme erased regional distinctions: Hungarian and Bohemian crowns were moved to Vienna and Latin replaced by German in administration.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Joseph saw himself as the servant of the state and was a rationalist, not a divine ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Joseph sought equal land tax; income tax was not at issue.

character-from-environment.rationale: Enlightenment thought and the belief that education and institutions improve people suggests this; inferred.
